en: The Apadāna of the Elder Minelapupphiya Kaṇikārapupphiya Chapter 2, Number 2 I offered a minela flower to the Buddha, the Teacher, who was endowed with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man. Because of that deed, I have been reborn in heaven for eighty-four thousand aeons. Having passed away from there, I was born here in the human world. I am now a monk, free from defilements, having attained the state of an Arhat. I have reached the end of suffering; there is no further existence for me. This is my final birth; I shall not be born again. This is my last body; I shall not take up another. Having performed this meritorious deed, I have now attained the fruit of Arhatship. “Golden-hued is the Blessed One,
possessing a hundred rays and full of majesty;
having ascended the walkway, he strides forth.”
With a mind of loving-kindness, like a peacock,
with a clear heart and joyful mind,
having paid homage to supreme knowledge;
Having plucked a *minela* flower,
I offered it to the Buddha.
Thirty-one eons ago from now,
Because I offered that flower in worship,
I do not know a state of misery;
this is the fruit of worshipping the Buddha.
In the twenty-ninth aeon,
one named Sumeghaghana,
endowed with the seven treasures, [will appear].
A wheel-turning monarch of great power.

In this way, indeed, the Venerable Elder Minelapupphiya recited these verses.
This is the second legend of the Elder Minelapupphiya.
